cluster_summary: A cluster of vulnerabilities where user-controlled wiki content is executed with the wrong security context (e.g., viewer's or page author's privileges instead of content owner's) or where missing required-rights analyses allow low-privileged users to inject script content that later executes with elevated privileges.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-controlled webhook URLs, callback URLs, endpoint parameters, or request destinations into outbound HTTP clients, URL.openConnection, fetch helpers, proxy clients, or webhook dispatchers. Report code paths where scheme, host, redirect target, DNS resolution, and private-address ranges are not constrained before the outbound request. Confirm that the guard is enforced before the sensitive effect and remains bound to the same resource, principal, destination, or object that the effect uses. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 1 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should enforce scheme and host allowlists, block private and metadata addresses after DNS resolution, and validate redirect targets.

mechanism.missing_guard: scheme, host, redirect target, DNS resolution, and private-address ranges are not constrained before the outbound request
mechanism.name: attacker-controlled webhook or callback URL fetch
mechanism.sink_shape: outbound HTTP clients, URL.openConnection, fetch helpers, proxy clients, or webhook dispatchers
mechanism.source_shape: attacker-controlled webhook URLs, callback URLs, endpoint parameters, or request destinations
mechanism.typical_fix: enforce scheme and host allowlists, block private and metadata addresses after DNS resolution, and validate redirect targets

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Explicitly pass the restricted flag to all derived contexts, or set it on documents.
sub_patterns.name: Missing propagation of restricted execution context flag
sub_patterns.root_cause: The security flag indicating restricted/sandboxed execution is not propagated to sub-contexts (transformation contexts, async jobs, field registrations, historical versions), causing content to be evaluated with default permissive privileges.
